articleTitle: Automotive Radar Simulator Based on Ray-Tracing and Machine Learning
abstract: In this paper, we have designed software that can simulate a driving scenario with several vehicles or pedestrians. Each target has 4 parameters: its type, speed, distance, and RCS. The software generates simulated signals using Ray-tracing and Neural Networks, which are trained with a real radar dataset. The Neural Network part uses a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) Network for Scenarios with more than two targets and a simple multilayer perceptron (MLP) network for simulating scenarios with just one target. After starting the simulation, it shows an animation of the movement of different targets on a road. In addition, it can save the radar signals received by the radar receiver and draw four plots from signals as the real location of targets in the Range-Doppler map (RD map), 1D FFT of the signal, 2D FFT image, and estimated location of targets. It can produce a defined number of random scenarios for dataset creation in machine learning research, while also considering the impact of antenna patterns on the received radar signals.

articleTitle: Three Degrees of Freedom Cells and a Perforated Dielectric for Wideband Reflectarray Fabrication
abstract: A self-covered, single-layer, inexpensive wideband reflectarray antenna is proposed using a class of Triangular Bowtie (TB) elements printed on interior side of a periodically perforated dielectric. Such an element has three degrees of freedom (air hole, angle, and length). Drilling periodic air holes within thick FR4 dielectric, the loss of unit cell is decreased. By changing the values of length, and angle of TB patch, two different phase diagrams are obtained that the sum of their ranges is more than 700°. With the help of such a unit cell, a center-fed reflectarray is designed and simulated. To validate the simulated results, a $270 \times 270 \times 3.9 \mathrm{~mm}^{3}$ array with focal length 26.1 cm is implemented and exactly tested. The achieved results by measuring reveal a bandwidth of 42.6% $(9.7 \sim 14.9 \mathrm{GHz})$ for $1-\mathrm{dB}$ gain, and peak gain value 29.1 dB with maximum efficiency 58% at central frequency 12 GHz.

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Adaptive Modulation in Medical Body Sensor Networks Using Visible Light Communication
abstract: In the context of medical body sensor networks that rely on visible light communication (VLC), adaptive modulation plays a crucial role. Despite VLC’s advantages, challenges arise due to fluctuating signal strength caused by patient movement. To address this, we propose an adaptive modulation system that adjusts based on link conditions, specifically the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Our approach involves an uplink channel for feedback, allowing the receiver to select the appropriate modulation scheme based on measured SNR after noise mitigation. The analysis focuses on various medical situations and investigates machine learning algorithms. The study compares adaptive modulation based on supervised learning with that based on reinforcement learning. By implementing a bi-directional system with real-time modulation tracking, we demonstrate the effectiveness of adaptive VLC in handling environmental changes (interference and noise). Notably, the use of the Q-learning algorithm enables real-time adaptation without prior knowledge of the environment. Our simulation results show that photodetectors placed on the shoulder and wrist benefit significantly from this approach, experiencing improved performance.

articleTitle: Shot Noise Optimal Filters for Phase-Diversity Homodyne Receivers
abstract: Analytical expressions for the signal to shot noise power ratio (SSNR) of phase diversity homodyne (PDH) optical fiber communication systems with arbitrary waveform and receiver filter are derived. The receiver filter structures maximizing the SSNR is calculated in closed form formulas. The SSNR performance of the systems is evaluated for rectangular and Gaussian pulse shapes and receiver filter structures such as matched filtering, the ideal integrator, and the photodetector RC model. As a side outcome, we show that the SSNR is upper-bounded by twice the converted electrons of the local oscillator. Numerical results show that the proposed optimal filter outperforms the ideal integrator and the integrator plus RC receiver by a few dBs. However, matched filtering to the complex received pulse amplitude is near optimal provided that the local oscillator power is much larger than the received power.

articleTitle: Classifying Benign and Malicious Websites through URL Feature Extraction Using Transfer Learning
abstract: With the rapid development of digital and communication infrastructures, Internet usage is expanding rapidly. As the global number of Internet users increases, so does the prevalence of cybercriminals and websites infected with various types of malware. Cybercriminals often exploit these infected websites to carry out their malicious activities. Therefore, identifying these websites is crucial to safeguarding Internet users. However, traditional blocklists provided by web browsing services remain ineffective in detecting zero-day attacks, highlighting the need for machine learning techniques in this area. In this paper, we utilize features extracted from URLs of both benign and malicious sites–including defacement, phishing, malware, and spam – to differentiate between the two categories. First, we transform the feature space, then perform feature extraction using pre-trained models such as ResNet50, SqueezeNet, and AlexNet. Finally, we classify the URLs using a long short-term memory (LSTM) deep neural network. This proposed method effectively mitigates the risk posed by four types of malicious websites. The simulation, implemented in Python, achieved an accuracy rate of 97.13%.

articleTitle: Evaluating LLM-Generated Persian Questions for Teaching Conditional Programming Using Bloom’s Taxonomy
abstract: The use of Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate educational content is increasingly becoming popular, but we still need to learn more about their effectiveness in non-English languages, especially for professional areas such as teaching computational concepts. Using Bloom’s taxonomy as a framework of assessment, this study evaluates the ability of LLMs to author Persian (Farsi) Learning Objects (LOs) for teaching conditional programming. We provided four LLMs (BloomGPT, Code Tutor, Copilot, and LLaMa) with a prompt in Persian to create educational questions and exercises to teach conditional programming structures to novice learners. A group of experts was asked to evaluate questions generated by LLMs based on their alignment with the specified level of Bloom’s cognitive domain, suitability for teaching conditional programming structures, and clarity in using Persian language. Results show almost no agreement among experts in language clarity and fair agreement on other aspects of the study. BloomGPT proves itself to be dominant overall in Bloom’s Taxonomy, especially at the “Analyze” level. Meanwhile, Copilot closely followed Code Tutor in most aspects of the study. Our findings provide insights into the ability of LLMs to design high-quality Persian learning resources in computer programming.

articleTitle: Ridge Waveguide Technology and Ridge Gap Waveguide Technology: A Comparison
abstract: Ridge Gap waveguide (RGW) has been a famous metallic transmission line in microwave and antenna technology applications since 2009. This structure has many advantages, that have outweighed its disadvantages, especially in high-frequency applications. However, the similarity of this technology to the ridge waveguide (RW) raised the question about the effectiveness of this waveguide in comparison to the RW. In this paper, the insertion loss of RGW and RW is compared. This comparison shows in terms of loss in Ku band there is no evident difference between them. However, RGW shows slightly better power handling capability compared to RW. Gysel power divider (GPD) has been designed, simulated, and measured in Ku band with both structures to have a proper comparison. Both power dividers covered the Ku-band, and even the lower side of K band was partially covered. The measured result of both structures showed good agreement with the simulation, which means both of them have low sensitivity to manufacturing error in the intended bandwidth; Another aspect of this research is that the manufacturing cost of RW is noticeably lower than RGW, which should be considered when one of these technologies is being considered for large-scale production.

articleTitle: Interference Precancellation in Multiuser Vector Broadcast Channels Using PSK Modulation
abstract: The low cost, energy efficiency, and resilience of constant-envelope modulations to power amplifier nonlinearity make them appealing for multi-antenna multiuser systems in 5G and beyond. This paper proposes a linear zero-forcing (ZF) and a non-linear ZF Tomlinson-Harashima precoder (THP) based precoding scheme for downlink multiuser MIMO systems with arbitrary-sized PSK modulation. The proposed scheme achieves perfect persymbol multi-user interference (MUI) cancellation, enabling high throughput with minimal delay, cost, and complexity. The precoder structure is relatively easy to implement, involving straightforward matrix calculations. Analytical and simulation results demonstrate that the MUI is perfectly cancelled, and the bit-error rate decreases unboundedly with increasing SNR.

articleTitle: An efficient design of a Crossbar Switch for Banyan Network and Nano Communication based on QCA technology
abstract: Quantum technology-based circuits process data a great deal faster than circuits built with conventional transistor-based technologies. Digital information in Quantum-Dot Cellular Automata (QCA) technology is provided by the polarization of electrons. One use of this QCA technology in the realm of nano communications is the construction of efficient electronic circuits. A collection of networked nanomachines with computing, data storage, sensing, and actuation capabilities is called a nanonetwork, often referred to as a nano-scale network. They can be constructed in a variety of methods, utilizing distinct stages for connecting connections and switching parts. Nanoscale communication network design reduces expenses and dissipation of energy. However, because the banyan network is one of the most widely used multistage communication architectural procedures that are required in all computer systems, it is also one of the most interesting issues in QCA nanotechnology. In this paper, a crossbar switch for banyan networks based on QCA is shown. The study suggests a single-layer, cost-analyzed QCA-based crossbar switch for the banyan network. The goal of the study is to reduce the number of cells, area, and latency in the crossbar switch for the banyan network that is based on QCA. The suggested QCA-based crossbar switch for the banana network uses 63 QCA cells, occupies $0.08 \mu^{2}$ of space, and requires a delay of 0.5 clock cycles to accomplish its objective. With the QCA Designer 2.0.3 program, the QCA-based crossbar switch for the banyan network is implemented.

articleTitle: Analytical Approach for Characterizing Discontinuity in Transmission Lines through Time-Domain Reflectometry (TDR) Method with Quadratic Loads
abstract: In this study, we aim to delve deeply into the theoretical basis of Time-Domain Reflectometry (TDR), specifically in the context of quadratic loading. Our primary objective is to conduct a comprehensive analysis to accurately determine a circuit’s inductance and capacitance. Furthermore, we intend to comprehensively analyze the TDR of two mismatched transmission lines. The goal of this analysis is to precisely calculate the impedance of the load and one transmission line, taking into consideration the impedance of the other transmission line.

articleTitle: Boundary Detection in Agricultural Fields Using a Residual U-Net++ Architecture
abstract: Agricultural land boundary detection with satellite imagery is really important for modern farming, especially in precise mapping, resource management, land changes monitoring, and violations controlling in agricultural areas. In order to accurately detecting field boundaries, this paper presents a new deep learning method that combines Residual U-Net and U-Net++ architectures for precise segmentation of farm fields. By mixing residual connections within a nested U-Net setup, the model improves feature extraction and refines field boundary detection. We used a loss function that helps with class imbalance, boosting segmentation performance. Tested on 1200 high-resolution aerial images from Catalonia, Spain, the model shows better results than existing methods, significantly improving field boundary detection. This method advances field segmentation technology and offers a valuable tool for precision agriculture.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network and ARIMA model to estimate ICT sector investment, a comparative approach
abstract: The purpose of this research is to predict the required ICT sector for the time period leading up to ١٤٠٥. The ICT sector was predicted based on Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN). The major difference between the results of the two models indicates the difference between these two methods in forecasting, and it was shown that the ARIMA model is not a suitable method for program-oriented forecasts because it is not possible to consider variables in its calculations like economic growth. On the other hand, the neural network method can provide a more reliable prediction due to the inclusion of the economic growth variable in the learning process.

articleTitle: A Traffic Control Approach to Minimize Congestion in O-RAN Architecture
abstract: The increasing traffic in densely populated areas has led to congestion issues in open radio access networks (O RAN). In this research, we address the problem of congestion in O-RAN and aim to minimize it utilizing mixed integer programming (MIP) techniques. Our focus is on the traffic steering between central unit (CU) and distributed unit (DU). In this way, we try to allocate the incoming prioritized packets to radio units (RUs) in a way that minimize the queue at DUs in an O-RAN architecture. We have developed an algorithm to transform the issue into a constrained multi-knapsack problem (MKP) and have introduced a solution to address it. The simulation results demonstrate that the presented algorithm can reduce the mean delay of packets up to $\mathbf{2 0 \%}$ respect to normal condition.

articleTitle: Multi-functional and multi-band reflective polarization converter based on an asymmetric metasurface in the terahertz band
abstract: In this study, we propose a multi-functional and multi-band polarization converter operating in the terahertz regime, based on an asymmetric metasurface. The polarization converter comprises a periodic array of unit cells, each consisting of a two-corner-cut square gold patch, a gold ground blocking sheet, and an intermediate polyimide dielectric substrate. The simulation results show that the proposed device functions as a cross-polarization converter (CPC) with over $\mathbf{9 0 \%}$ efficiency across three frequency bands of $0.43 \sim 0.51 \mathrm{THz}$, $0.66 \sim 0.89 \mathrm{THz}$, and $1.35 \sim 1.39 \mathrm{THz}$. Moreover, it serves as a linear-to-circular polarization (LP-to-CP) converter in four distinct frequency bands of $0.34 \sim 0.43 \mathrm{THz}, 0.51 \sim 0.66 \mathrm{THz}$, $0.89 \sim 1.35 \mathrm{THz}$, and $1.39 \sim 1.45 \mathrm{THz}$, maintaining an axial ratio (AR) below 3 dB. The normalized ellipticity of the reflected wave, indicative of circular polarization handedness, approaches ±1 within these operating bands. The converter’s multi-functionality and simple structure make it promising for biomedical applications, particularly in terahertz imaging.

articleTitle: Proposing a Novel Assessment Framework for Evaluation of Public Cloud Service Providers
abstract: This paper introduces a novel assessment framework designed for evaluating public cloud service providers. The proposed framework distinguishes between long-established companies with substantial physical infrastructure and emerging smaller firms that require supportive policies and incentives. It evaluates providers on two aspects: technological capabilities and innovation. In this framework, the primary indicators is structured around six key criteria: Legal, Physical Infrastructure, Active Cloud Service Infrastructure, Services and Applications, Business, and Security. Also, the supplementary indicators is based on service panel and innovation. Evaluation indicators and their weights are proposed based on a thorough review of existing standards and benchmarks. To validate the framework’s applicability, we applied it to assess five cloud service providers in Iran alongside three major international providers. The evaluation results demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework in ranking public cloud service providers. Keywords-cloud computing, cloud service provider, criteria, assessment, framework.

articleTitle: Capacity Maximization for Double Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface-Assisted MIMO System
abstract: Using Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) instead of traditional relay systems represents a significant advancement in wireless communication technology. RIS can intelligently manipulate radio signals by adjusting phase shifts, thereby improving signal quality and energy efficiency. This study investigates the effectiveness of the Dimension-wise Sinusoidal Maximization (DSM) algorithm in a MIMO multi-user system with dual RIS. The results show that increasing the number of RIS units significantly enhances telecommunication capacity and reduces energy consumption compared to configurations with a single RIS.

articleTitle: QoT Estimation of a Commercial DWDM Transmission System Using Artificial Neural Network and Its Feature Importance Analysis
abstract: In this paper, we proposed an artificial neural network (ANN) architecture to estimate the optical signal-to-noise ratio (OSNR) of an in-use commercial dense wavelength-division multiplexing (DWDM) system. The model yields a very close estimation of the values the optical spectrum analyzer measured during periodical maintenance measurements (mean absolute error is less than $\mathbf{0. 0 4}$ for OSNR values in dB). Since our model is based on periodic measurements, it represents an updated network state. Furthermore, to investigate the compliance of the ANN model with previous theoretical studies, we have examined the importance of the features. The results imply that complex and accurate models like the ANN model for in-use commercial systems do not necessarily behave as the theoretical analyses suggest. This is due to the complex nature of quality of transmission (QoT) analysis in optical systems and other factors such as equipment aging and errors not included in the theoretical studies. Feature importance analysis could help in simplifying the models based on network specifications by removing features with low impacts while maintaining the required estimation accuracy.

articleTitle: Detection of Customer Satisfaction in In-Person Telecommunication Services Using Automated Facial Image Analysis with Artificial Intelligence
abstract: In the present era, improving customer experience and enhancing services in the telecommunications industry are of paramount importance. One of the fundamental criteria for evaluating customer experience is their level of satisfaction with services at physical sales points. This paper focuses on the automated analysis of facial images using artificial intelligence to determine the satisfaction level of inperson visitors to telecommunications service booths. Advanced technologies such as transfer learning and the use of the EfficientNet network architecture have been employed to provide a more accurate and efficient method for facial emotion analysis. The results of this study demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves the accuracy and efficiency of emotion detection and, consequently, the satisfaction or dissatisfaction of visitors in both implementation stages. This research not only contributes to the improvement of service processes and the enhancement of customer experience but also confirms the superiority and reliability of this method by comparing the results with previous approaches. These findings can assist telecommunications businesses in improving services and increasing customer satisfaction, guiding them towards optimized performance and success. This study is introduced as a solution for improving the customer experience process during in-person visits to telecommunications service offices, which has extensive applicability in enhancing communication systems, increasing employee productivity, improving service delivery supervision and management, and enhancing responsiveness and service quality at telecommunications service counters. Additionally, it provides for increased customer satisfaction and loyalty, optimization of internal company processes, improved marketing strategies, and more accurate assessment of customer experience status.

articleTitle: Optimizing Smart Parking Solutions in Vehicle-to-Vehicle Networks
abstract: In the era of smart cities, the demand for efficient traffic management systems has surged, particularly for smart parking solutions. This study investigates the integration of vehicle-to-vehicle communication technologies in locating available parking spaces through a practical implementation using mobile devices. We propose a novel approach employing a non-dominated multi-objective genetic optimization algorithm combined with learning automata to enhance the parking search process. The results indicate a significant 20% reduction in the time required to find parking, demonstrating the effectiveness of our algorithm in real-world scenarios. This research contributes to the advancement of intelligent transportation systems by providing a scalable solution for urban parking challenges.

articleTitle: Multicore Photonic Crystal Fiber Plasmonic Sensor
abstract: In this work, due to the importance of photonic crystal fibers (PCFs) in sensing and biosensing applications, three plasmonic PCF structures are investigated as refractive index sensors. The PCF cores are provided near the interface with the surrounding medium so that by adding a noble metal layer on the PCF, the evanescent field of the cores can excite the surface plasmons of the metal. The plasmonic PCFs are immersed in different analytes with different refractive indices to detect the variation of analyte refractive index. These three structures are investigated to determine the effect of the number of cores on the sensing properties of the plasmonic PCF. By various calculations and also simulation with finite element method (FEM), the best characteristics of the PCFs are obtained. We have found that the optimum structure is the double-core PCF plasmonic sensor with sensitivity of 2333.33 nm per refractive index unit (nm/RIU), figure of merit (FOM) of $110 \mathrm{RIU}^{-1}$, and sensor resolution of 0.00214. This sensor has a linear response with 99.7% accuracy to detect the refractive index of biological materials. Therefore, such a sensor can be useful in biomedical diagnosis and environmental monitoring applications.

articleTitle: Local Graph Convolutional Network for Hyperspectral Target Detection
abstract: A graph convolutional network (GCD) is suggested for hyperspectral target detection in this paper. To extract the spatial neighborhood information in each local region of the hyperspectral image, to extract latent spectral relationships among neighbors and to explore the irregular class boundaries corresponding to each local patch centered at the pixel under test, a small local graph is constructed for each pixel. After several graph convolutional blocks for exploration of spectral-spatial latent dependencies, the label of each pixel is predicted in the last layer. The GCD with composing a local graph correspond to each pixel and its spatial neighbors can well enhance discrimination among target and background, which leads to significant improvement in the detection results. The experimental results show superiority of GCN compared to convolutional neural network (CNN) and several other hyperspectral target detectors.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a THz Topological Frequency-Tunable Waveguide based on Valleytronics
abstract: In this work, we present a THz waveguide based on topological photonics, specifically utilizing the valley degree of freedom (DOF). Our device is designed to operate in two distinct frequency ranges: 0.7 to 0.9 THz and 1.4 to $\mathbf{1. 6}$ THz. The design is based on a 2D honeycomb lattice of silicon rods with a lattice constant of $100 \mu \mathrm{~m}$. This lattice structure allows for easier fabrication than more complex topological photonic structures. By breaking the inversion symmetry of the unit cell, we induce topological energy gaps and generate oneway edge states. We have demonstrated that these edge states are robust against kinks in the waveguide, achieving transmission efficiencies of over 90%. Additionally, we have studied how the distance between the two photonic crystal regions (VPC1 and VPC2) affects the transmission spectrum and the dispersion of the topological edge state. Increasing this distance flattens the edge state, indicating the potential to create slow-mode waveguides. The unique properties of our topological THz waveguide, such as backscattering-resistant propagation and the ability to tune frequency response, make it a promising candidate for next-generation high-capacity wireless communication systems. We believe this design approach could be valuable for developing THz demultiplexer components.

articleTitle: Classification of Congestive Heart Failure Disease, Arrhythmias, And Normal Heart Rhythms Using Deep Learning
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases, regardless of their causes, are considered one of the most important causes of death worldwide. For this reason, the issue of time is critical in diagnosing cardiovascular diseases. If a heart disease is diagnosed in a patient by a doctor promptly and then the prescribed solution for treating the disease is properly implemented, not only will it prevent the end of life, but it will also greatly improve Quality of life for people who are facing this issue heart diseases. Given the limitations and challenges in diagnosing cardiac diseases from normal sinus rhythms, the presentation of automated machine learning methods is essential. This article aims to present an efficient method for classifying congestive heart failure disease, arrhythmias, and normal heart rhythms using a combined network of convolutional neural networks and gated recurrent unit networks (CNN+GRU). For this purpose, in the first stage, a dataset consisting of electrocardiogram (ECG) signals in three groups of normal sinus rhythm, congestive heart failure, and cardiac arrhythmias was extracted from the Physio-Net database, and preprocessing and noise removal of the signals was performed. In the second stage, continuous wavelet transform has been used to convert ECG signals into two-dimensional matrices. In the third stage, classification was performed using a combined model of convolutional neural networks and gated recurrent unit networks. Finally, the results obtained from two methods, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and a combined approach of Convolutional Neural Networks and Gated Recurrent Unit (CNN+GRU), have been compared. The results have shown improvement, reduction of errors, and a significant increase in the accuracy of the proposed method in classifying congestive heart failure from other arrhythmias and normal heart rhythms.

articleTitle: A Novel Electronic Voting system using a Blind Signature scheme and Blockchain
abstract: Many applications including government services are now available online. This allows people to access services without being physically present, but online authentication is required. An important online service is electronic voting which can significantly increase the participation rate due to time limits and the removal of location restrictions. Electronic voting protocols employ encryption algorithms to ensure the integrity of the voting process. Despite the many advantages of electronic voting, it is controlled by the system manager and a dishonest manager can compromise the voting integrity. Blockchain technology can be used to solve this problem by providing reliability and data integrity. In this paper, an electronic voting scheme is proposed which employs quantum collective blind signatures and blockchain to guarantee privacy and the integrity of the voting process.

articleTitle: Lateral movement detection through a heteregenous GNN model of kernel-level log
abstract: Lateral movement is a technique for complex attack scenarios such as Advanced Persistent Threat (APT) that the attacker moves laterally from one machine to another one and can infect all networks or systems of the organization. One of the ways to identify this threat is to check the kernel-level $\log$ for investigating the behavior or activity of a user who makes the processes and events that are suspicious. From the relationships between different processes and events and their characteristics, a malicious activity can be identified, which can indicate the presence of an attacker. Therefore, regarding this point of view, we form a Heterogenous Graph Neural Network (HGNN) by considering these relationships. We apply the proposed method on the public labeled kernel-level $\log$ of BETH dataset that gathered in 23 honeypots. We reach $\mathbf{9 9. 4 \%}$ accuracy and evaluate the HGNN model by precision and recall. This is a good result to detect the presence of an attacker with a lateral movement behavior.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Compact Metasurface With Polarization Rotation For Reflection-Transmission Modes
abstract: This paper presents a compact dual-band metasurface with polarization rotation performance including U-shaped strips to rotate polarization of electromagnetic wave into its orthogonal counterpart in transmission and reflection modes. To demonstrate the proposed U-shaped unit cell mechanism, an equivalent circuit analysis is employed. The proposed polarization converter is able to rotate left-handed circularly polarized wave (LHCP) into right-handed one in transmission-mode at the bands of 11.3 GHz and 17.6 GHz. Moreover, right-handed circularly polarized wave (RHCP) can be converted to LHCP in reflection-mode at 11.3 GHz and 17.6 GHz. Additionally, despite of increasing the incoming angle of incident wave, the response of the proposed design is able to be almost stable up to 40°. At the symposium, details of the polarization rotation procedure, and comparison to previous works will be exhibited.

articleTitle: Two-Dimensional Slot Array on a Nonplanar Gold film Metasurface, Designed for Melanoma Skin Cancer Detection
abstract: A THz metasurface is designed and proposed for early demand in biomedical technology, particularly in cancerous cells detection. The Two-dimensional slot array on a nonplanar gold film metasurface is presented to operate at THz frequency band. The nonplanar gold film is placed on a silica (SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) substrate and excited by a THz plane wave source from the bottom side. The outcomes by the CST finitedifference time-domain (FDTD) solver demonstrates the reflection coefficient of less than -13 dB at the center frequency of 4 THz, and achieves the realized gain of about 13 dBi at a 0.2 THz bandwidth. The resonance frequencies at the available bandwidth are related to the properties of the skin cell sample, and help to evaluate, and conclude the presence of cancerous cell.

Author Keywords: Two-dimensional Slot array on a nonplanar gold film Metasurface

articleTitle: Exploring Feature Map Correlations for Effective Fake Face Detection
abstract: In recent years, the internet and social media platforms have seen a massive influx of data, particularly images. To effectively identify fake content, we employ a deepfake detection technique aimed at determining the authenticity of uploaded material. In this paper, we achieve fake face detection with high accuracy by utilizing deep feature map relations. Our approach leverages transfer learning techniques from pretrained deep models, such as VGG16, VGG19, and ResNet50. We analyze the generated Gram Matrix of each layer, where deep feature relations are similar to the covariance matrix, reflecting correlations between different feature maps. These features are used to classify content as fake or real using a simple CNN, and the results are reported and compared. This study explores deep feature map relations as crucial indicators for detecting inconsistencies introduced by image generators. By employing pre-trained networks, we analyze and explore feature map relations generated in each layer as higher-order quality features. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed inconsistency detection feature yields satisfactory results. The entire implementation of this work can be found at https: //github.com/hnarges91/Fake-Face-Detection.

articleTitle: Graph Signal Processing Meets Optical Resource Allocation
abstract: Graph signal processing is an emerging field in which traditional signal processing tools from regular Euclidean domain are adapted for use in irregular domains such as graphs. This paper demonstrates how graph signal processing can be used as an efficient tool to solve an optical resource allocation problem, particularly the routing and wavelength assignment problem, where a reduction of 25% in blocking probability can be achieved compared to the conventional counterpart schemes.

articleTitle: RHC-Based Systematic Design of a Wide-Angle Periodic Coded THz Reflectarray
abstract: A reflectarray designed by Random Hill Climbing (RHC) optimization process is demonstrated and simulated. On the basis of top layer effect on reflection phase and exploiting the relation between phase distribution and the direction of the reflected beam, six pixelated subcells are optimized for two incident angle waves simultaneously. The far field plot shows that for beams of incident angles 19.471° and 41.81° and in the precincts of them the reflectarray deflects the incident waves into reflections close to normal to the reflectarray surface. This shows a proximate independency of incident wave angle for the reflectarray in a certain angular range. The proposed cells provide 342° reflection phase range. Also, the reflection loss of the cell for the incident angles 19.471° and 41.81° are -1.9 dB and -1.4 dB, respectively. The pattern gain and fractional bandwidth for a finite reflectarray of size $300 \lambda \times 150 \lambda$ are reported to be 19.44 dB and $\mathbf{2 5 \%}$ for the incident angle 19.471°, and 19.17 dB and $\mathbf{3 0 \%}$ for the incident angle 41.81°.

articleTitle: Outdoor Visible Light Positioning using Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: In this study, 2-D positioning is examined in a 60 $\text{m} \times 5 \text{m}$ area using a Visible Light Communication (VLC) link employing urban lighting infrastructure, the so-called Infrastructure to Vehicle (I2V) scenario, where a deep learning-based method is applied for this purpose. In this work, 4 photodiodes are used in the receiver. Also, 3 street lights in a row are considered as three transmitters. As a result, 12 received power signals from three transmitters are used for four receivers to estimate the position. The results obtained using the proposed architecture show an improvement in average positioning error of up to $37 \%$ compared to similar works, under various scenarios including different transmitter distances, road widths, and transmitter heights. This performance improvement varies depending on the mentioned parameters, with the positioning error increasing as the distance between transmitters increases. Additionally, in these study, the channel conditions, signal transmission, and reception are considered much closer to reality compared to similar works, although the signal transmission method used is simpler. The cost of this improvement is an increase in computational complexity and doubling of the positioning computation time compared to the similar work where the deep network architecture used is of the Multilayer Perceptron type.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning for AoI-aware Transmission Control in Energy-Harvesting Grant-Free NOMA IoT Networks
abstract: The advent of Internet of Things (IoT) networks has revolutionized various real-time applications, such as healthcare, smart cities, and remote automation, by enabling seamless data exchange and real-time monitoring and control. Real-time applications require fresh data, which is quantified by a novel metric, Age of Information (AoI), defined as the time elapsed since the generation time of last successfully received data. Additionally, due to energy limitations in most IoT scenarios, the trade-off between age and energy becomes an important challenge in these networks. Motivated by the need to optimize both data freshness and energy efficiency, this paper considers a real-time scenario in energy-harvesting (EH) IoT networks that operate based on grant-free (GF) Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) mechanism. Given the foresighted nature of the transmission control problem due to the stochastic dynamics of the AoI and energy charging processes, we introduce a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework that dynamically manages transmission decisions and resource block allocation, minimizing the average sum AoI across IoT devices, while considering energy feasibility. Through extensive simulations, we demonstrate that our proposed DRL-based approach significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of expected cumulative cost, showcasing its potential for enhancing the performance of future IoT networks.

articleTitle: End-To-End Performance For User-Centric Cell-Free Mmimo Networks With Multiple CPUs
abstract: Cell-free massive MIMO network, as a promising solution for future wireless communication systems, is conven-tionally equipped with a single central processing unit. In this paper, we multiply the number of central processing units in a user-centric cell-free massive MIMO network and demonstrate its impact on communication efficiency. Specifically, we show that under a fair comparison scenario in terms of complexity and cost, having two central processing units increases the fronthaul data rate and the end-to-end peak data rate by up to 47% and 6%, respectively, compared to the conventional situation, where a single processing unit is assumed.

articleTitle: Simulation of Cell Movement Control by Magnetophoretic Chips
abstract: Magnetic nanoparticles have attracted a lot of attention in various fields, including engineering and medicine. Magnetophoretic and Microfluidic chips are a suitable tool in laboratory systems for localization, Precise control of particle movement, composition, manipulation and investigation of magnetically labeled cells. Recently, inspired by electronic circuits for the controlled transfer of particles on a chip in a magnetic field, magnetic circuits have been introduced in which a capacitor-like model is used to store cells and a diode-like model is used to store cells. Transistor cell transfer method is also used for switching (transfer of the selected cell). Thus, single-cell studies are a new field that has had many impacts on cell biology in the past years. Advances in this field require systems capable of precisely controlled magnetic cell movement. In this research, in order to obtain a multiple array for the addressable transfer of cells with magnetic label, in order to investigate the cell transfer in 90, 270 degrees bends in the TI transfer path with disk pattern and I strip, simulation has been done. A multiple array is then designed. The pattern of the injection site in the TI tracks is also designed to avoid the initial deviation of the cell on the magnetophoretic chips to reach the intended main track.

articleTitle: The cost of renting a fiber network from one operator to another
abstract: With the expansion of optical fiber under the 13th government, the coverage has increased from approximately 1.5 million households in 2021 to more than 8 million households by 2024. It has also been decided that by 2025 the amount of coverage will reach about 20 million households. In Iran, the expansion of the fiber optic network in each sector is the responsibility of a single operator. Therefore, as the fiber optic network expands, the demand for network service providers to rent fiber from network owners to provide service to households increases. Because of this issue, the discussion of fiber optic network rental pricing is very important. In this research, the rent of each part of the fiber optic network has been determined. First, to determine the rental price, the cost of fiber optic network development was investigated in three segments: the Feeder Segment, the Street Cabinet, and the Distribution Segment, across metropolitan areas, provincial centers, and other cities. The results show that the fiber optic developer operator spent $1,2.7$, and 4.8 million Tomans per user in metropolitan cities, provincial centers, and other cities, respectively. Then, by using two cost-benefit methods and the Depreciation cost method with a fixed rate, the minimum tariff for sharing optical fiber between two operators was estimated. The results show that the minimum monthly sharing tariff in metropolitan cities, provincial centers and other cities for each subscriber should not be less than $3,5.1$ and 14.4 thousand tomans in the fixed rate depreciation method, respectively, and this monthly sharing tariff in the cost-benefit method as well In metropolitan cities, provincial centers and other cities, per subscriber should not be less than 30,53 and 145 thousand tomans, respectively. The reason for the high difference between these two methods is that in the depreciation method with a fixed rate, the sharing tariff must be adjusted and increased every year based on the inflation rate, but in the cost-benefit method, the inflation rate during 20 years is an average of 25% and The profit of the network owner is also considered to be around 11%, and there is no need to increase the minimum sharing tariff during the 20-year effective life of the network.

articleTitle: Blockchain Security Threats: Survey
abstract: Blockchain technology has seen extensive application across various sectors since its introduction. The rise of cryptocurrencies, such as Bitcoin, and smart contracts have significantly enhanced the security and efficiency of digital systems through blockchain. Nevertheless, an in-depth examination of blockchain security remains necessary. This paper systematically reviews the security threats to the blockchain, examines real-world attacks, and proposes countermeasures to enhance the technology’s security. The goal is to aid in developing more secure blockchain systems and highlight future research directions in this area.

articleTitle: Introducing a Semantic Model for Smart Composition of E-Learning Content
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive survey of expert opinions on integrating semantic Artificial Intelligence (AI) in digital education, focusing on the conversion and composition of Learning Objects (LOs) to support diverse educational contexts. It highlights the role of semantic computing in bridging the semantic gap between human cognitive processes and machine operations, facilitating more intuitive and context-aware human-computer interactions. Through structured qualitative interviews with experts, the study explores the interoperability and modularity of LOs as defined by the IEEE Learning Object Metadata (LOM) Standard, categorizing them into Action and Object classes to better align with instructional purposes. The findings underscore the importance of semantic AI in enhancing educational content’s personalization and adaptability, demonstrating its potential to transform digital learning through more effective, scalable, and human-centered educational tools. This research provides insights into the evolving role of semantic AI in education, emphasizing its capacity to enhance learning experiences by enabling the meaningful collaboration of educational content authors and AI technologies.

articleTitle: A Bibliometric and Visualization Analysis of Research Trends and Hotspots on Digital Economy Diplomacy
abstract: Digital economy diplomacy is an important topic that has received much attention in recent years. Determining key topics and the relationship between them is very important in this field. This study aims to investigate and evaluate the current research trends and directions in the field of digital economy diplomacy using bibliometric analysis. In this way we have distinguished 9 main clusters with digital trade as a central cluster.

articleTitle: GN-CNN-LSTM: Financial Market Prediction With Gaussian Noise Embedded CNN LSTM
abstract: Accurate financial market prediction is challenging due to volatility and complex patterns. This study presents a novel approach that injects Gaussian noise into a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model, enhancing prediction accuracy. While denoising techniques such as Autoencoders, Wavelet Transform, Filtering Techniques, and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) are commonly used, this research demonstrates that injecting noise during preprocessing significantly improves the performance of the CNNLSTM model. Empirical results using historical data show that the CNN-LSTM model with injected Gaussian noise outperforms traditional models, with notable improvements in MAE and RMSE metrics. Specifically, in SHOMP, SHI, HSI, and XAUUSD, the value of MAE in different sequences improved to $0.017,0.052,0.030$, and 0.021, respectively, highlighting the effectiveness of the GN-CNN-LSTM model. These findings underscore the potential of noise-injected deep learning models, instilling optimism for achieving more reliable financial market predictions.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Challenges and Opportunities of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Iran’s Banking Industry
abstract: The Fourth Industrial Revolution involves the shift in the economy and society that has been driven by emerging technologies. Among these are Artificial Intelligence and other related scientific innovations. This paper explores the effect of Generative Artificial Intelligence on the Iranian banking industry using a SWOT analysis. The results indicate that the identified opportunities are more than threats the existing, while weaknesses are more than strengths, so the industry falls into the WO quadrant. Consequently, it is recommended that banks adopt a Redirection strategy utilizing Generative Artificial Intelligence.

articleTitle: Broadcast beam synthesis in an 8T8R array in TDLTE and Sub-6GHz 5G band
abstract: Beamforming is an inseparable part of the technologies used in 5G base station antennas due to the increased wireless data traffic and mobile users. Among commonly generated beam types, the broadcast beam is one of the main beam types of today’s base station antennas. This paper presents a simple method to synthesize and generate 65° broadcast beam in different frequencies from 2.3 to 3.8 GHz. The proposed method has been implemented on an antenna array of four ±45 polarized crossed-dipoles, and the resulting beams are in accordance with the corresponding theory. The results show that one can design a 4-column array with various typical beamwidth values ranging from 50 to 90 degrees, including 65 degrees, which is the paper’s target. The limitation enforced by lateral element distance and their element pattern is studied as well. In some frequencies, 65° patterns were not achieved using the procedure of the presented method due to the effect of element distances and the element beamwidth, which is discussed in the paper. To solve this problem, the method of using asymmetrical weighting is examined successfully, obtaining higher achievable beamwidths.

articleTitle: Improve Quality of Systems via Dynamic Cost-Aware Selection of Web-Services
abstract: Due to the dynamic performance of web services, a pivotal step in ensuring the quality of our system is dynamic service selection. The study aims to reach a more precise objective function for the problem and improve it by considering the cost of service selection. The method we propose takes into account the expenses associated with service selection by executing the service selection process to determine the optimal services solely in instances where there is a notable change in service metrics. To gather the data required for evaluating this work, we used a virtual server provided by Hetzner Online GmBH and collected information about round-time trip by using the global ping network. By implementing this method, we lower the number of service selections, which might slightly decrease the quality of service. We believe our method could lead to a higher overall score in objective function.

articleTitle: Analytical Performance model for Hyperledger Fabric for Communication Technology use cases
abstract: Due to increasing usages of the blockchain solutions in communication technology, and considering the real-time nature of these use cases, it is required to develop an analytical performance model of blockchain based solutions. To this end, in this paper an analytical delay model of the Hyperledger fabric blockchain is developed. To provide this model, the techniques of the network calculus are employed.

articleTitle: Signal Detection Using Compressive Sensing in Massive MIMO Systems with multidimensional Modulation
abstract: Large-scale multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) has been recognized as a major technology for wireless communication systems. In massive MIMO systems, detection is a main issue because there are a large number of antennas at the base station in comparison to traditional MIMO systems. While multidimensional modulation is effective in minimizing interference and simplifying detection, it has not been utilized for detection in massive MIMO systems. This work introduces a novel detector for large-scale MIMO systems using multidimensional modulation. We model the system with sparse signal sources and propose an approximate Maximum Likelihood (ML) relaxed detector that minimizes the Euclidean distance to the received signal while maintaining a constant $\ell 1$-norml. The proposed method offers a balance between accuracy and computational efficiency, making it well-suited for systems with sparse structures. Simulations show that the proposed detector achieves optimal performance and outperforms the other method.

articleTitle: Array of Conformal Cavity-Backed Slot Antenna With Switched Beam Pattern for IoT Devices
abstract: In this paper an array of conformal antennas with switched beam patterns is presented. The array antenna consists of three $\mathbf{U}$-shaped cavity-backed slots, mounted on a cylinder. The proposed antenna has a 5.5% fractional bandwidth in the ISM band of 433 MHz. This ISM band is used in Internet of Things (IoT) devices and smart city applications. The cavity-backed structure of the proposed antenna increases the antenna gain while the conformal shape increases the half-power beamwidth. Each antenna of the proposed scheme has a gain of about 3 dB and a saddle radiation pattern with a half-power beam width (HPBW) of $\mathbf{1 2 0}$ degrees. Therefore, three examples of the proposed antenna can cover the $\mathbf{3 6 0}$-degree horizon with the beam switch network. The cylinder shape of the proposed antenna is suitable for urban traffic lights in smart traffic control systems. The proposed antenna is simulated with both time and frequency domain techniques using CST software, where results are greatly matched in both simulations.

articleTitle: NOMA-SWIPT optimization with PSO and machine learning algorithm
abstract: This research aims to optimize energy efficiency (EE) in telecommunication systems by focusing on a combination of non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) and simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT). The Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm is employed, leading to significant improvements in energy efficiency compared to existing methods. Our findings demonstrate that PSO effectively optimizes multiple parameters, achieving higher energy efficiency. Additionally, a Random Forest-based machine learning (ML) model is introduced to enhance optimization speed.

IEEE Keywords: Simultaneous wireless information and power transfer

articleTitle: Interaction Between Power Allocation and BER Performance for mCAP-NOMA in Visible Light Communication
abstract: In this work, we investigate a combination of multiband carrierless amplitude and phase (m CAP) with nonorthogonal multiple access (NOMA) in visible light communication (VLC) networks, which can be a suitable candidate for the next-generation of mobile networks. Our study includes a theoretical analysis of a two-user m CAP-NOMA scheme and a comparison between two well-known gain ratio power allocation (GRPA) and the fixed power allocation (FPA) methods. Simulation results indicate that our system model, combined with the GRPA method, outperforms the FPA method in terms of bit error rate (BER) performance. This improvement is observed in scenarios where users are either both static or when one user is static and the other is mobile. Moreover, our results indicates that the user located at a greater distance from the optical access point (AP) achieves lower BER compared to the user placed at a shorter distance to the AP.

articleTitle: Public Safety Assessment of Radio Frequency Electromagnetic Exposure
abstract: With the rapid growth of wireless communication systems, the public concerns about possible health effects of exposure to electromagnetic radiations are increased. This paper investigates the results of measured exposure levels of radio frequency (RF) emission in the rural areas. The sources of emission include all RF emitters from broadcasting stations to cellular base stations. The power density measurements were conducted during 1 year at 680 locations distributed over major cities. The results were compared with the relevant guideline for non-ionizing radiation given in Iran national standard no. 8567, to confirm that the measured radiation exposure levels are satisfactorily below defined limits.

articleTitle: Implementation Sentences Attention Mechanism in Online Reviews
abstract: Sentiment analysis involves recognizing the opinions expressed within a piece of text. Sentiment analysis classifies comments as positive, negative, or neutral. The Majority of researchers in this field are based on word-level attention. We believe sentences are an important part of the text, therefore, they must have different weights. Hence In this paper, we introduce a sentence attention mechanism (SAM) that utilizes multi-head self-attention to enhance the performance of sentiment analysis models by effectively capturing contextual relationships within sentences for improved interpretability and accuracy in classification tasks. We carried out multiple sentiment analysis experiments across various domains, including multi-domain, cross-domain, and domain-specific approaches, using real-world datasets. The results of these experiments demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms other basic models and achieves higher accuracy. The accuracy of the model is 0.68

articleTitle: A Hybrid Local Linear Neuro-Fuzzy Model for Digital Transformation Scenario Analysis
abstract: Organizations typically implement digital transformation by creating and assessing several scenarios based on factors that gauge how well the organization aligns with development methodologies. In the decision-making field of digital transformation, where the environment is complicated, it is essential to employ highly effective ways to prioritize scenarios. This article utilizes a hybrid method that integrates fuzzy, neural networks, and metaheuristic algorithms to help decision-makers make optimal choices. In order to mimic the selection process for projects, a hybrid model is created by merging Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) with the Local Linear Neuro Fuzzy System. The study’s findings show that the suggested strategy and the created method produce better and more accurate evaluations.

articleTitle: Developing 3D CAD Models and Low-Cost Hardware for Learning New Topics in Telecommunication Laboratories
abstract: Amidst the COVID-19 pandemic, the learning and teaching of various laboratory skills encountered numerous challenges. In electrical engineering, the field of telecommunication involving fields and waves requires the creation of different devices and their subsequent measurement in laboratory settings. In the undergraduate curriculum of this field, the antenna and microwave laboratories play a crucial role in acquainting students with tangible devices, their operational mechanisms, measurement specifications, and the utilization of measurement equipment. To facilitate the comprehension of courses related to microwave devices and antenna design, a compilation of 3D designs was devised to simulate performance alongside theoretical concepts. This extensive collection includes components like transmission lines, waveguides, couplers, filters, circulators, antennas, and more. It serves as a valuable resource for traditional in-person theory classes and provides a foundation for research projects undertaken by graduate students. It can be used to generate a database for use in designs with the help of machine learning, too. Subsequently, several pieces of educational hardware were designed and constructed to address emerging topics, including automotive radar, software-defined radio, and spread spectrum telecommunications.

articleTitle: Optimizing Urban Traffic Flow in Smart Cities: A Fuzzy Goal Programming Approach
abstract: The integration of new technologies, such as cloud computing, internet of things and artificial intelligent is essential for enhancing urban traffic management systems. This research aims to develop a comprehensive model for determining traffic volume in smart cities. An optimal planning algorithm was employed to analyze data, seeking the most effective solution from a set of alternatives. The proposed algorithm utilizes fuzzy weighting based on the average distance of vehicles approaching traffic lights, allowing for the determination of optimal timing for each light section. The results indicate that the algorithm outperforms fixed-time traffic lights, achieving a 15% reduction in urban traffic congestion. improvement being about 15% compared to the normal state.

articleTitle: A New Method to Improve NDN Forwarding Packets Using SDN
abstract: In recent years, the growth in advances in various communication and information technologies has led to the development of Named Data Networking (NDN) and Software Defined Networking (SDN). NDN simplifies data dissemination with features like name-based delivery and in-network caching, while SDN allows for centralized programming and management of network components. Integrating NDN with SDN creates an intelligent, flexible network that enhances communication quality, forwarding decisions, and resource management. This paper proposes a method to improve NDN routing. It examines the role of the Forwarding Information Base (FIB) and the number of active entries in NDN nodes concerning content retrieval delay. Then, by integrating NDN with SDN, the centralized control plane of SDN is used to improve routing decisions. By monitoring the load of active entries in the FIB table in NDN nodes and directing packets through optimal paths, the study investigates methods to reduce content retrieval delay and increase the number of data packets entering nodes. Simulations using the ndnSIM simulator show that the proposed scheme reduces delay and increases content retrieval efficiency.

articleTitle: Challenges of Artificial Intelligence Technology and Its Impact on Digital Economy Growth
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology has a huge impact on the process of development related to the digital economy. This paper is derived from some country experiences to establish the key challenges the world is facing in regards to AI, which pertain to inequality and discrimination, unemployment issues, and changes in the labor market. Further, this article also investigates further to determine the direct and indirect effects of those challenges within the digital economy. Despite the significant opportunities that AI offers to increase productivity and innovation, managing these challenges requires multifaceted approaches and careful policy making. Finally, this article has emphasized the importance of investing in infrastructure, training skilled workforce, developing appropriate laws and increasing transparency and trust in the use of AI to fully utilize the potential of this technology for the sustainable growth and development of the digital economy.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a High-Efficiency 5W Ku-Band Power Amplifier Using a Bare Die GaN HEMT for Satellite Uplink Applications
abstract: This paper presents a Ku-band 5W Power Amplifier (PA) using a bare die Gang high electron mobility transistor (HEMT). The circuit was implemented using microwave-integrated circuit (MIC) technology. Wirebonds have been implemented using $\mathbf{2 5}$-micron gold wire on a Rogers 4003C substrate with a thickness of 0.1 mm. Simulation modeling of wirebonds was validated using passive test circuits. Experimental results demonstrate that the PA operates in the 12.5 to 13.5 GHz frequency range, with output power, drain efficiency, and gain of higher than $5 \mathrm{~W}, 40 \%$, and 5 dB, respectively under continuous wave (CW) operation, which is suitable for uplink satellite communication applications.

articleTitle: A machine learning-based approach for multi-class intrusion detection and classification in IoT using CICIoT2023 dataset
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is a set of physical devices connected to the Internet that collect information from the operating environment and share it with users or other devices. One of the most important challenges in IoT is the security of connected devices; they are vulnerable to attacks and infiltrations and traditional Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) often fail to overcome this problem. In this article, six machine learning models, including Logistic Regression, AdaBoost, Perceptron, MLP, Random Forest and Hist-Gradient Boosting, are used to solve this problem. These models are trained on the recently available CICIoT2023 dataset and are used to classify attacks for three different classification modes of binary, eight and 34 classes. The performance of the models is evaluated based on several evaluation criteria such as accuracy, precision, recall, f1-score and training time. Evaluation results suggest that the Random Forest algorithm achieves the best classification results with test accuracy $=0.9955$, while the Hist-Gradient Boosting algorithm has the best performance in terms of training time.

articleTitle: Exploring Fourier Neural Operators for Electromagnetic Scattering
abstract: This paper proposes a novel learning framework to address electromagnetic scattering. Although conventional full-wave numerical methods, such as the Method of Moments (MOM), are effective, they are computationally intensive. On the other hand, machine learning-based algorithms can offer real-time solutions, but they are often limited by the extent of their training data. To integrate physical knowledge into neural network architectures, we employ neural operators, specifically the Fourier Neural Operator (FNO), to enhance data efficiency and accuracy in electromagnetic simulations. Our modified FNO model, trained on various dielectric distributions, achieves accuracy comparable to state-of-the-art architectures like UNet, but with less data. This framework bridges the gap between physics-based knowledge and data-driven approaches, paving the way for faster and more adaptive simulations.

articleTitle: Key Performance Indicators in Information Sharing and Analysis Centers (ISAC)
abstract: The Information Sharing and Analysis Center (ISAC) were established to gather, analyze and share of received alerts from SOC’s or other threat gathering tools. What is shared in the ISAC is the result of knowledge derived from the analysis of incoming alerts. This knowledge helps other subscribers of the information-sharing ecosystem to improve their incident handling and network security status. These systems enhance the organization’s network security and reduce the response time to incidents. Today, they have become one of the most important foundations of security, playing a vital and important role in managing threats and updating strategies. To ensure the effective performance of ISAC centers, it is essential to evaluate various aspects of their methods for collecting, analyzing, and sharing information. In this context, key performance indicators (KPIs) serve as valuable metrics for assessing the performance of Information Sharing and Analysis Centers (ISACs) across various dimensions. This research identifies essential KPIs within three core modules: information collection, analysis and sharing. The study is grounded in established standards, relevant literature and expert interviews. It also takes into account the five dimensions of Global Cybersecurity Index (GCI) in ITU. This approach ensures that the all final 77 identified KPIs are both relevant and significant. Finally, the contribution of each of the modules and dimensions of GCI in the key performance indicators of ISAC centers will be determined. Ultimately, this study will connect the contribution of each ISAC architecture module and dimension of GCI to the KPIs. The results of this classification are significant for the management levels of ISAC centers, as they enable a proper evaluation of the performance of various modules, prioritize resource allocation and refine evaluation methods.

articleTitle: EngageMe: Enhancing Academic Performance While Watching Video Learning Objects Using Visual Modifications
abstract: Keeping learners engaged and improving academic performance are essential challenges in online educational environments. Since Video Learning Objects (VLOs) are being widely utilized, engaging learners, especially during the initial moments of viewing, is an essential factor in their effectiveness.This study investigates the impact of various audiovisual modifications on learners’ attention and academic performance, mainly focusing on the first 20 seconds of educational videos. The goal is to determine which modifications most effectively capture and sustain attention to improve learning outcomes.The experiment consisted of four video blocks, the first of which was an unmodified baseline video. The following three blocks were subject to changes in screen brightness, background color, and white noise. Academic performance was assessed through multiple-choice questions designed to measure comprehension and retention, focusing on the initial 20 seconds of each video.The study found that all three modifications positively influenced attention and academic performance compared to the baseline. Among the modifications, color changes were the most effective, significantly increasing attention during the first 20 seconds of the video. Although still more effective than the baseline, white noise and brightness changes had a less pronounced impact.The findings suggest that strategic audiovisual modifications can enhance the effectiveness of VLOs by improving learner attention and academic performance. In particular, color change is proposed as a powerful tool for capturing early attention.

articleTitle: Synthetic Collision-Prone Trajectory Data Generation Using CTGAN for Connected Autonomous Vehicles
abstract: The safety and reliability of connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs) hinge on their ability to navigate complex and unpredictable driving environments. Traditional testing methods, relying on real-world data and simulations, often fall short of providing the diverse and comprehensive set of collision scenarios needed for rigorous evaluation. On the other hand, mobility trajectory data acquisition is challenging due to privacy concerns, commercial considerations, missing values, and expensive deployment costs. This paper presents a novel approach to generating synthetic collision-prone trajectories using the Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Network (CTGAN). By leveraging CTGAN’s ability to handle imbalanced and mixed data types, we create a rich synthetic dataset that enhances the validation and testing processes for CAVs. Our methodology includes the preparation of real-world trajectory data, the configuration and training of the CTGAN model, and the generation of a diverse set of collision-prone scenarios. We test our approach using two large-scale real-world trajectory datasets and comparative analyses with other trajectory generation methods, including TimeGAN and SocialGAN, to underscore the superiority of our approach in generating realistic and varied scenarios. This research contributes to the field of autonomous vehicle testing by offering a robust and scalable solution for scenario generation. The synthetic dataset not only improves safety and reliability metrics but also provides a valuable resource for future research and development. Our findings suggest that integrating CTGAN-generated data into CAV testing frameworks, not only in terms of statistical and quality metrics, is better than the other approaches but also can significantly enhance the preparedness of autonomous vehicles, ultimately contributing to safer and more efficient transportation systems.

articleTitle: A Sparse Multistatic Circular Array for Millimeter-wave Imaging System
abstract: In this paper, we address the problem of millimeter-wave imaging using a multistatic circular array. Circular array provides uniform omnidirectional beamforming, and simplified beam steering with the ability of full 360-degree coverage. It offers less grating lobes compared to planar arrays which improves signal quality. In this work, we focus on designing a sparse structure while maintaining the concept of the circular array with the objective of scanning the top view of the human body. The design is based on the compressed sensing model which allows us to design a very sparse structure. The proposed structure includes two sparse rings that use only 10 transmitters on one ring and 20 receivers on another ring. In total, 93.32% element reduction comparing a uniform double-ring array with a maximum SLL equal to $-7.71 \mathbf{d B}$ is achieved. The simulation results support our design and using the developed CS model, successful reconstruction has been obtained with a PSNR of more than 10 dB compared to the conventional recovery method.

articleTitle: Removing Speckle Noise from Synthetic-Aperture Radar Images Using Artificial Intelligence Techniques
abstract: In recent times, Synthetic-Aperture Radar (SAR) images have gained significant importance due to their extensive use in both military and civilian applications. However, these images are often compromised by speckle noise, which severely hampers their interpretability and utility across various domains. This paper explores a range of image denoising techniques, with a particular focus on deep learning-based approaches, while also considering traditional methods. Given the critical nature of the subject, real SAR images have been rigorously analyzed. The study emphasizes that speckle noise in real SAR images is far more detrimental than in simulated scenarios, revealing the limitations of artificial intelligence algorithms when used in isolation for denoising tasks. To address this challenge, the proposed algorithm in this paper first preprocesses the real data using classical methods before applying a neural network for denoising. Both quantitative metrics and visual assessments demonstrate that this hybrid approach not only outperforms standard denoising methods but also preserves critical information in SAR images more effectively.

articleTitle: Proposing a Comprehensive Method for Extracting Monitoring Indicators for Cloud Service Layers
abstract: With the rapid expansion of cloud services within organizations, effective monitoring and oversight of performance, security, and availability have become crucial. This paper begins with an analysis of various methods for extracting cloud service monitoring indicators, focusing on the requirements and metrics essential for a Cloud Services Monitoring Center. We review and compare different techniques for extracting Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) across cloud services, highlighting the strengths, challenges, and specific applications of each method. Based on this evaluation, we propose a hybrid approach for extracting monitoring indicators tailored to different cloud service layers, aiming to establish a robust Cloud Services Monitoring Center. For the Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) layer, we recommend methods such as network traffic analysis, log monitoring, and telemetry. For the Platform as a Service (PaaS) layer, we suggest API-based, event-based, and AIdriven methods. For the Software as a Service (SaaS) layer, we identify agent-based and container-based approaches. This hybrid framework is designed to address specific needs, leverage available resources, and meet operational objectives effectively. Keywords- Monitoring, Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), Cloud Service, Hierarchical model.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Electromagnetic Metamaterial Inverse Design
abstract: Designing metamaterials involves computationally intensive tasks, resulting in a time-consuming design process. A deep learning approach is proposed to generate metamaterial designs directly from the input S-parameter diagram. Furthermore, to address the challenge of creating the input diagram, a fine-tuned Large Language Model (LLM) generates the S-parameter diagram based on user input prompts. Compared to traditional neural network methods, the use of an image-based deep learning network enhances the architecture by minimizing the pre and post-processing steps required to transform a metamaterial unitcell image into an numerical array, and vice versa. Simulation results confirm the agreement between the generated metamaterial and the desired input response.

articleTitle: Wide-Band Dual-Polarized BTS Antenna Using Crossed-Dipole with Parasitic Elements
abstract: This study introduces a novel design of dual-polarized antennas for BTS applications. It features four identical parasitic-elements placed above the crossed-dipole arms, which enhances the antenna’s impedance performance. This design reaches an operational bandwidth of 1.481-2.717 GHz for port-1 and 1.495-2.773 GHz for port-2. The interaction between the dipole arms and the parasitic-elements ensures proper impedance matching within the frequency range of BTS systems working in the $1.7-2.7 \mathrm{GHz}$ spectrum. Experimental results indicate that the proposed design achieves a peak gain of 8.36 dBi at 2.50 GHz. Furthermore, the half power beam width (HPBW) of the antenna measures 97.14° in the elevation plane and 65.02° in the azimuth plane.

articleTitle: DOA Estimation in FMCW Automotive Radars with Interference: ML and VMD Approaches
abstract: In this paper, we deal with the problem of estimating the Direction of Arrival (DOA) of vehicles under the interference assumption in frequency division multiplexing-multiple input-multiple output (FDM-MIMO) Automotive radar systems. To estimate the DOA, we propose two approaches. In the first approach, with the help of a designed machine learning network, waveforms that are associated with interference are identified and excluded from the MUSIC algorithm for the DOA estimation. In the second approach, instead of removing the waveforms contaminated with interference, we use the variational mode decomposition (VMD) technique to reduce the interference of the waveforms. Finally, the DOA is estimated with the help of a novel weighted-MUSIC algorithm whose weights are determined based on the signal to the interference ratio (SIR) output from the VMD algorithm.

articleTitle: Analytical Performance model for Sliced 5G core network
abstract: Providing an upper bound of the service latency in communication networks is a key step of validating service provisioning. Due to the different types of the services that may be provided by the 5G network, it is very critical to calculate their upper bound of latency according to different configuration of the network. In this paper, an upper bound of the service latency for 5G core network with sliced UPF function is provided using network calculus.

articleTitle: Design a Multi-layer Dielectric Lens with Beam Scanning Capability for 5G Communication System
abstract: This paper proposes a multilayer dielectric lens with a non-uniform permittivity coefficient. This lens can be placed in front of a base antenna to steer the 5 G band antenna beam direction. A method for combining the host dielectric layer with air in a multilayer structure has been used to achieve different permittivity coefficients in different parts of the lens. The simulation results for the proposed structure suggest that it is feasible to achieve the base antenna beam scanning in the range of $\mathrm{- 21}$ to $\mathrm{+ 21}$ degrees at $\mathrm{30} \mathrm{~ GHz}$ frequency. The main principle in this dielectric lens is the antenna gain variations deficiency over the beam scanning range. So, the maximum gain variation over the entire beam scanning range is less than 1 dB which is equivalent to about 5% of the total gain. The proposed multilayer lens structure requires less effort and time for the manufacturing process thereby having a lower cost compared to other perforating-based dielectric lens manufacturing methods.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable and Tunable Iris Filter Based on Plasma Technology
abstract: This paper presents a novel tunable and reconfigurable bandpass iris filter integrated within a standard rectangular waveguide, utilizing plasma technology. The proposed filter employs plasma slabs to create iris structures that enable dynamic control over the center frequency and bandwidth of the filter. When the plasma slabs are inactive, the filter behaves as a conventional waveguide, while activation allows for tuning the characteristics of the filter by adjusting the excitation current applied to the plasma tubes.
