abstract: Nowadays, retweeting behavior is considered a substantial behavior to analyze information diffusion in the microblogging network. To understand the underlying mechanism of information diffusion and analyze the evolution of the diffusion corresponding to a given original microblog, user retweeting behavior prediction has recently gained considerable attention. In this paper firstly, we introduce the most influential factors which affect user retweeting behavior and propose an effective measurement based on the random walk model to measure the social influence. Secondly, by incorporating our defined influential factors into a logistic regression classifier model, we predict the future activated user set concerning the diffusion of a given original microblog at the next time point. Unlike other comparative models, our prediction model can illustrate the evolution of diffusion and predict the retweeting behavior of all potential users through the diffusion of any original microblog in the microblogging network. Finally, based on the real Twitter microblogging dataset, the experimental results show by the contribution of our defined influential factors and presenting an effective measure of the social influence factor, we can obtain more accurate predictions in comparison to other baseline methods.

articleTitle: A Consulting System for Portfolio Assets Allocation by Selecting the Best Agent in the Short Term Based on Cumulative Returns with Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a sophisticated consulting system designed to optimize investment portfolios using deep reinforcement learning (DRL). The system includes a unique decision-making mechanism that selects the best-performing agent in the short term based on cumulative returns. We employ five different DRL agents: Advantage Actor-Critic (A2C), Soft Actor-Critic (SAC), Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3), Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG), and Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), to allocate portfolio weights dynamically. By evaluating each agent’s performance over the previous ten days, our system adaptively selects the agent most likely to maximize returns in the immediate future. This approach enhances portfolio performance by leveraging the strengths of multiple DRL agents. The effectiveness of our proposed method is validated using historical data from the Dow Jones index, demonstrating significant improvements in cumulative returns and risk-adjusted performance metrics. Our results show that the main proposed method achieved the highest annual return of 11.43%, cumulative returns of 38.29%, and a Sharpe ratio of 0.832, outperforming individual DRL agents and highlighting the potential of DRL in advancing portfolio management strategies.

articleTitle: Smart Border Wall Condition Monitoring Using Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) Sensors
abstract: Observing and monitoring the country’s borders by human forces has disadvantages such as people’s negligence, limited field of vision, camouflage of the enemy in different ways, and life risks. Therefore, border control requires an intelligent, accurate, and highly sensitive system. Today, with the advancement of technology, many sensors have appeared. One of these sensors is based on the technology of “Fiber Optic Bragg Grating” (FBG) sensors. Present technology has received special consideration in the recent years because of its unique features. Optical fiber sensors have a special and significant advantage over other sensors due to their use over long distances and fast data byte transmission, as well as the effective sensitivity of these types of sensors to changes in their surrounding environment. Also, the applications of these types of sensors are economical, and by using optical fiber cables containing sensors along the border lines on the surface, the depth of the ground, or inside border barriers such as border walls, they can carefully monitor and control the physical changes in the environment in all parts of the borders of the country. The secondary goal of this study is to develop a machine-learning model capable of distinguishing outdoor events across three specific categories by examining the mirrored graphic representation of the shape of a wave waveform from the FBG sensor and classifying the outcomes into one of the defined categories. This article is a report on the proposal of the practical application of Indigenous technology of optical fiber Bragg (FBG) sensors in the “Iran Telecommunication Research Center’, which is used in the form of deployment inside the border wall as embedded sensor elements.

articleTitle: Detecting Human Attention States Exploiting an Intelligent Approach Combining Fuzzy Inference System and Support Vector Regression
abstract: In recent years, one of the main issues in e-learning has been the personalization of educational content for learners. Identifying cognitive factors that influence learning plays a significant role in improving the performance of personalization systems. “Attention level” is one of these factors. Given the absence of a teaching agent in the e-learning environment, detecting learner attention in this context is very complex. Therefore, designing intelligent systems that can detect learner attention and provide appropriate educational feedback is very important. This research estimates individuals’ attention levels by analyzing “head movements.” To this end, the head pose angles, including Pitch, Yaw, and Roll, were estimated using the Support Vector Regression (SVR) algorithm and optimized through a Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm. Following these three metrics considered input variables for the fuzzy inference system, a system was designed to estimate attention levels. Applying this system to the AFLW2000 dataset yielded an accuracy of 86%, which significantly outperformed previous studies.

articleTitle: From Policy to Innovation: A Comparative Analysis of Digital Economy Strategies in Selected Countries
abstract: This article presents a comparative analysis of the digital economy strategies of the Arabian Union, European Union (EU), and China using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) methodology. The study assesses these strategies based on four key indicators: Policy and Regulatory Framework, Digital Infrastructure, Innovation and Technology Adoption, and Human Capital and Skills. The findings reveal that the EU leads in overall digital economy readiness, driven by its strong regulatory environment, advanced infrastructure, and emphasis on human capital development. China, while excelling in digital infrastructure and innovation, faces challenges in regulatory frameworks and workforce skills. The Arabian Union, though currently in the early stages of digital transformation, shows significant potential for growth, particularly with ongoing investments in infrastructure and strategic initiatives like Saudi Vision 2030. The analysis highlights the strengths and areas for improvement for each region, providing valuable insights for policymakers aiming to enhance their digital economy strategies and global competitiveness.

articleTitle: Providing the Optimal Structure of Computer Emergency Response Teams Based on Service And Process
abstract: Today, with the growth and development of information technology, infrastructures and information systems in an organization are based on cyber space. According to the definition of non-operational defense organization, cyber space is interdependent networks that consist of information technology infrastructure, communication networks, computer systems, controllers of critical industries, virtual environment, information and interaction between this environment and humans in order to produce, Process, store, exchange, retrieve and exploit information is useful, but it is prone to many risks. As a result of negligence and failure to take care of the threats of this network, it is possible to lose information and assets. In order to respond to incidents in this regard in the shortest possible time, it is necessary to set up a team to respond to computer security incidents in every organization; So that the network can be controlled and unauthorized attacks and intrusions can be detected in a reliable platform. It also increased the response speed in the shortest possible time with optimal communication between components. For this purpose, in this research, relying on the method of comparative studies, the required data were extracted in this regard. Then, regarding the structure, services and processes of cert centers, questions were formulated and raised in the field survey meetings with experts in this field; The results of this analysis are presented in this research article in the form of a favorable situation by providing a service-based structure and examining the main processes of these centers. In this document, after presenting the organizational structure, this structure has been re-divided based on the type of services and the units responsible for providing these services have also been specified in this proposed model. In the following, the steps and operational processes of each of these units have been introduced.

articleTitle: Countering Physical Adversarial Attacks in Semantic Communication Networks: Innovations and Strategies
abstract: In the evolving landscape of telecommunication systems, the emergence of semantic communication networks presents both opportunities and challenges, particularly in the face of physical adversarial attacks. This article explores innovative strategies to enhance the resilience of semantic communication systems against such attacks, leveraging advanced machine learning techniques and robust data encoding methods. Inspired by the behavior of natural noises, we implement a model and integrate it into our semantic network, and to improve classification accuracy, we transfer our analysis to the text. By analyzing existing vulnerabilities and proposing novel countermeasures, we aim to provide a comprehensive framework that not only improves the security of semantic communications but also enhances their efficiency and reliability. Our findings reveal that integrating adversarial training and semantic-aware encoding can significantly mitigate the impact of physical attacks, thereby paving the way for more secure communication infrastructures.

articleTitle: LLM Performance Assessment in Computer Science Graduate Entrance Exams
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly utilized in educational settings, raising questions about their efficacy in standardized testing contexts. This study evaluates the performance of popular LLMs, including GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Flash, Llama-3.1-70B, Mistral Large 2, DeepSeek-V2, and Gemma-2-27B, in answering data structure and algorithm design questions from the Iranian university entrance exams for master’s programs in computer science and information technology. The research analyzes the accuracy of responses, the length of answers, required reading time, and vocabulary levels across the 2022,2023, and 2024 exams. Questions were categorized into five main areas: Algorithm Analysis and Complexity, Sorting and Searching, Graph Algorithms, Data Structures, and Advanced Topics and NP-completeness. The study compares the LLMs’ performance in both Persian and English contexts, providing a comprehensive evaluation of their capabilities and limitations in this domain. Results indicate that GPT-4o achieved the highest average accuracy ($\mathbf{7 5. 0 \%}$), followed by Claude 3.5 Sonnet (67.2%) and Mistral Large 2 (64.1%). The majority of the models performed better on English questions compared to Persian, with GPT-4o showing the largest performance gap (81.3% vs $\mathbf{6 8. 8 \%}$). The findings offer insights into the practical applications of LLMs in educational assessments and contribute to the ongoing discourse on the role of AI in academia, particularly in non-English speaking regions.

articleTitle: Decentralized Federated Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for Energy-Efficient Base Station Switching Control
abstract: G cellular networks have achieved significant improvements in capacity and performance, while they have incurred a substantial increase in energy consumption at the base station (BS) level. To address this escalating energy consumption in dense 5G networks, this paper proposes a decentralized federated learning (DFL)-enhanced Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) framework for intelligent BS switching. Our approach leverages the distributed nature of 5G networks to collaboratively learn optimal BS on/off policies without centralized control. By combining DFL with DRL, we enable efficient knowledge sharing among BSs while maintaining privacy and reducing communication overhead. The cost function designed in this paper aims to balance energy savings as well as Quality of Service ($\mathbf{Q o S}$) requirements. Moreover, to enhance exploration and accelerate convergence, we incorporate an exploration network into the DRL agent and adopt a novel approach of model training. Performed simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework in achieving significant energy reduction of over 23% and total cost of 19%, while maintaining satisfactory QoS performance compared to the existing methods.

articleTitle: An overview of the components of digital transformation from the perspective of models and frameworks presented in international reports
abstract: Systematic evaluation of actions and strategies for achieving and developing the country’s digital economy, national information network, and other major activities in this field is essential. Given the extensive impact and influence of information and communication technology, a comprehensive understanding of the components of the digital transformation phenomenon at the national level is undeniable. One of the best solutions to access the components of digital transformation is to leverage international experiences in this field. The models and frameworks presented in international reports serve as suitable references for understanding the influential components of digital transformation. These components themselves encompass multiple indexes, each with several indicators to assess the current conditions. Therefore, studying the proposed models and frameworks in international reports on digital transformation can provide sufficient knowledge of these components. This research focuses on examining the components of digital transformation in several models and frameworks presented in international reports on digital transformation.

articleTitle: Analyzing The Impact Of Sleep Quality On Cognitive Abilities Using Game-Based Assessment
abstract: Mental ability, which is the core of the learning process, is under the effect of different lifestyle factors like sleep quality. Prior research has explored the general relationship between sleep and various physical and mental abilities, including its impact on memory consolidation, problem-solving, and emotional regulation. This study investigates the impact of sleep quality on cognitive performance across some specific cognitive domains. Our main goal is to find the relation between the sleep quality and task performance, followed by analytical consideration, lead to predict cognitive outcomes. This research integrates quantitative analysis of sleep and performance data collected from Health Watch with assessments of cognitive tasks. Participants’ sleep quality was monitored and analyzed using personal data collection tools, providing a comprehensive dataset for examining the subtle nuances of sleep’s impact on cognitive tasks. The findings reveal a correlation between sleep quality and performance in memory, speed, and language games, which were used to measure participants’ cognitive abilities related to the respective tasks. These findings underscore the potential for personalized sleep strategies to enhance cognitive performance. This research expands possibilities for improving cognitive strategies through better sleep practices, offering valuable guidance for educators, students, and cognitive scientists in tailoring sleep and performance interventions.

articleTitle: Optimum Patch Selection for Wideband Planar Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons Ku-Band Satellite Receive Antenna
abstract: Three single line linearly polarized planar leaky wave (LW) spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPP) Ku-band satellite reception antennas with circular, square and rectangular radiating patches are presented and compared. A novel method for feeding patches with an open-ended standing wave (SW) SSPP waveguide is also used. All three antennas are simulated by CST Studio commercial software, and the best patch type is selected by comparison of the results. SSPP-LW planar KU-band antennas are finding wide applications in 5G, 6G, existing Geo-stationary (GSO) satellites and emerging non-geostationary (NGSO) satellite constellations communications. The high gain needed for most of these applications in practice, dictates utilization of an array of several branches of antennas, resulting few hundreds of patches. Therefore, any improvements due to optimized selection of patch type studied in this letter, has significant importance in the overall antenna performance. Moreover, the optimized structure is a wise selection for the main building block of large high gain planar LW-SSPP antenna arrays.
